decisions.note: R1: maker's baseline spec used a dead-end duplicate warning; client supplied the reference-correct behavior (route to edit the existing bookmark).
R1: baseline auto-capture was title-only; client requested favicon + description that maker never surfaced.
R1: maker explicitly put import/export out of scope, contradicting reference items; client rejected that exclusion.
R1: baseline spec lacked case-insensitive search, quoted-phrase exact match, and tag-scoped search; client requested all three.
R1: only newest-first sort existed; client asked for a user-selectable alphabetical option.
R1: baseline had delete-only; client asked for reversible archive distinct from permanent delete.
R1: baseline spec had no unread/read-later concept; client requested it.
R2: spec lacked tag autocomplete; client asked for suggestion-on-entry to avoid near-duplicate tags.
R2: spec had no bulk action concept; client requested select-many + tag/archive/read/delete in one action.
R2: import description only covered title/address; client supplied the reference-correct detail (folders->tags, original date preserved).
R2: notes had no formatting; client asked for markdown (bold/list/link) with rendered display.
R2: no saved-search/bundle concept existed; client requested it (with 'not a big lift' hedge).
R3: bulk actions were manual-selection only; client asked for 'apply to whole filtered/matching set.'
R3: only single-tag filtering existed; client asked for multi-tag OR-include and NOT-exclude combination.
R5 plan gate: maker offered keep/drop on saved-search feature; client selected 'keep,' the reference-preserving alternative (a real fork since 'drop' would have diverged).
R10: shipped build defaulted every new save to unread, inverting the 'deliberate shortlist' semantics of read-later; client supplied the correct default (read unless flagged).
R11: bulk actions shipped with add-tag but no remove-tag, though REF-BM-20 names both; client asked for the missing half.
